text:
Maya Gupta: Escalation from ACME — sudden p99 spike for streaming responses starting ~45m ago. They say non-streaming endpoints are normal. Customer impact: UI stalls for long polls.

deploy-bot: [ALERT] svc-ingress: p99_streaming_latency > 1.5s (5m) for tenant=acme-prod — triggered at 1766548800

Leo Chen: I'm looking at edge logs now. Quick check: streaming TTFB vs total?

Maya Gupta: They reported TTFB specifically — first-chunk delayed. Total tokens still in range when it arrives, but first-byte waits ~800ms p99 (was ~90ms baseline).

Ash Patel: Noted. Any recent release to runtime or edge coalescing heuristics? I deployed the small-batching change to edge yesterday that tweaks chunk coalesce window from 8ms -> 12ms for CPU savings.

Samir Roy: That matches symptoms (longer buffer window => delayed first flush). But why only for ACME? Could be path-specific — their requests hit a high-load edge pool with coalescing enabled.

Leo Chen: I can repro locally with a synthetic streaming request through the same edge pool. Command I used:
```
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  "https://api.redwood.dev/v1/generate?model=rw-large&stream=true" -d '{"prompt":"hello\n","max_tokens":128}'
```
Getting ~700ms to first chunk when edge coalesce window set to 12ms and low-opportunistic-flush.

Ash Patel: Add logs from runtime:
```
[2026-03-17T15:02:11Z] chunk_flush_decision: window_ms=12, queued=1, last_kv_present=true
[2026-03-17T15:02:11Z] emit_chunk delayed_by=610ms reason=coalesce_window
```

Maya Gupta: Customer attached a trace showing request path: edge-us-east-1 -> ingress-proxy -> runtime-dedicated-3. Edge shows # of requests spike at same time.

Samir Roy: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Force streaming->non-streaming fallback for ACME (they accept non-stream UX), 2) Flip coalesce window back to 8ms on the affected edge pool, 3) Add tenant override to flush-first-chunk-immediately.

Maya Gupta: They prefer to avoid non-streaming if possible. Can we do an edge config revert to 8ms for acme-prod?

Leo Chen: I can patch edge config per-tenant. Quick test: pushed tenant-override coalesce_window_ms=0 (force immediate) to canary for acme-dev. Repro shows TTFB back to ~60ms.

Ash Patel: I agree we should roll a targeted rollback for the coalesce change on the affected edge pool. Simpler than feature toggle work. I'll prepare a canary rollout to acme-prod only.

deploy-bot: [DEPLOY START] edge-config-rollout coalesce-window-revert -> canary for tenant=acme-prod by Ash Patel (1766549150)

Leo Chen: While that rolls, add metrics: first_chunk_time_ms tagged by tenant and route. Also instrument the flush_reason field in logs so we can see coalesce vs size-trigger.

Ash Patel: Can do. Pushed a logging patch and config revert to canary (1766549205). Monitoring dashboard shows p99 TTFB drop from 800ms -> 80ms in canary traces.

Maya Gupta: ACME confirmed improvement on canary path after test. They want full prod patch.

Samir Roy: Safety checks: run 30m canary, check CPU/RPS delta (coalescing reduced may increase load). If within thresholds, promote. Also add quick fallback: allow tenant header `x-rw-stream-warm` to force immediate flush if customers opt-in.

Ash Patel: Can do full promote at 1766549300 if canary holds. I'll annotate the change in release notes.

deploy-bot: [DEPLOY PROMOTE] edge-config-rollout -> prod for tenant=acme-prod (1766549350) by Ash Patel

Leo Chen: After promote, p99 TTFB for acme-prod normalized. I'll keep alerting muted for this tenant for next hour and track regressions.

Maya Gupta: Thanks all. Action items:
- Ash: Rollout promoted, add tenant override documented (assigned)
- Leo: Add flush_reason metric and dashboard panels
- Samir: Add temporary alert tuning for tenant-specific anomalies
- Maya: Follow up with ACME ops once monitoring stable

Ash Patel: noted — will open PR with config diff and include rollback playbook.

Maya Gupta: Closing the escalation after 1h of stability unless new hits. :white_check_mark:
